{"answer":"“Dense to sparse” retrieval can be done by extracting sparse, BM25-compatible features from dense retrievers, or by training learned sparse retrievers that approximate dense semantic matching while using inverted-index search.

Latent Terms shows that dense retrievers trained for inner-product scoring can be decomposed into “retrieval-ready sparse features” using Sparse Autoencoders, producing a latent vocabulary with Zipfian statistics that is directly suitable for classical sparse scoring via BM25. This sparse decomposition can match or outperform single-vector scoring from the base dense model and SPLADE variants. [2]

Alternatively, learned sparse retrievers can be trained end-to-end from dense-leaning representations into sparse models: SPLARE trains Sparse Autoencoder-based learned sparse retrieval to produce semantically structured sparse features optimized for retrieval, outperforming vocabulary-based learned sparse retrieval in multilingual and out-of-domain settings. [7] LACONIC similarly trains learned sparse retrievers with a two-phase curriculum to bridge performance with dense models while reducing index memory. [1]

These differ in mechanism: Latent Terms focuses on extracting BM25-ready structure from an existing dense retriever, while SPLARE/LACONIC focus on training sparse retrievers directly (with sparse autoencoders or a Llama-based sparse retriever). [2, 7, 1]","grounded":true}
